'''Translations of SWCCG''' are the language editions of Star Wars CCG. Decipher printed the English game from 1995 through 2001. Takara printed Japanese sets. Further language editions were planned, including German-language and Spanish-language releases, and were later cancelled.<ref name="encyc">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf SWCCG Collecting Encyclopedia 3.2], p.201 (Other Foreign Language Releases). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009141805/https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf Wayback, 9 October 2026]. Collecting hub: [https://www.starwarsccg.org/collecting/ starwarsccg.org/collecting/].</ref>

== Japanese ==

Takara printed Japanese Premiere Limited in April 1997 (black border; 基本カード): 15-card packs and 60-card starters with a Japanese rulebook. Product photos and the Japanese [[Help Me Obi-Wan Kenobi]] Effect-template printing are on [[Premiere Limited]]. Japanese A New Hope, Hoth, and both Two-Player games followed. Encyclopedia 3.2 also records that anime-style cards were considered for Japan and were not released.<ref name="encyc" />

== Cancelled German release ==

Queens Games was in charge of the German translation. The company pulled the contract after Japanese sales, and the edition was not released. Surviving artifacts are 1998 magazine advertisements (''Offizielles Star Wars Magazin'' #8–#11) and a Modern Graphics German two-player rulebook. The full account is on [[Cancelled German release of SWCCG]].<ref name="boardmatt-jp">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1tdmHYND4xc Star Wars CCG - Japanese Card Overview], BoardMatt, guest Andy Talaga (3 April 2022). Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-1tdmHYND4xc Internet Archive]. Advertisement frames: [[:File:OSWM_German_Premiere_ad_BoardMatt_2022.png]]; [[:File:OSWM_German_Premiere_booster_spread.png]].</ref><ref name="boardmatt-col">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4dR5MIPH4h4 Star Wars CCG - Most Interesting and Strangest Things in Our Collections with Special Guest Andy], BoardMatt, guest Andy Talaga (29 May 2022). Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-4dR5MIPH4h4 Internet Archive].</ref>

German players promoted and won the English game. [[Philipp Jacobs]] of Germany won the [[1997 Decipher World Championship]]. [[Bastian Winkelhaus]] of Germany won the 2001 replacement Worlds at FreedomCon. Decipher Squadron Members in Germany included Winfried Sommerfield in Bochum (Red 41 FL), Michael Krause in Aachen (Red 67), Michael Lierheimer in Langenbach (Red 102), and Lars Malcharek in Duisburg (Red 114).<ref name="sm" />

== Cancelled Spanish release ==

Encyclopedia 3.2, under Other Foreign Language Releases, records additional language releases planned beyond the Japanese sets. Those further languages were not released. The photographs on that encyclopedia page are Japanese Takara packs.<ref name="encyc" />

Decipher prepared a Spanish-language [[Premiere Two-Player Introductory Game]] rules booklet for that impending Spanish release. The surviving printer proof, dated 2 July 1998, is on [[Spanish Premiere Two-Player Game rules booklet]].<ref name="fb-sergio">[https://www.facebook.com/groups/starwarsccg/permalink/10159018539903127/ SWCCG Two-Player Game Rulesbook (Spanish).pdf], Sergio Domenech, Star Wars CCG Facebook group (8 September 2021). Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/swccg-spanish-2pg-rules-booklet-1998 Internet Archive]; [[:File:Spanish_Premiere_Two-Player_Game_rules_booklet.pdf]].</ref> Decipher's May 1999 product library lists the English Premiere Two-Player Introductory Set and does not list a Spanish SKU.<ref name="library">[https://web.archive.org/web/19990504174938/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/productlibrary/thecollection/index.html Star Wars Customizable Card Game : The Expansions], Decipher.com product library (archive, 4 May 1999).</ref>

Decipher Squadron Members in Spain promoted the English game: [[Sergio Domenech]] in Madrid (Red 49 FL), Guillermo Ruiz in Barcelona (Red 42 / Gold 17), and Unai Herran in Zaragoza (Red 48).<ref name="sm">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/decipher-swccg-squadron-members/ Decipher SWCCG Squadron Members], starwarsccg.org. Fan-site table: [https://www.geocities.ws/plarathas/SMs.html geocities.ws/plarathas/SMs.html]. Preserved copies: [https://web.archive.org/web/20160409152825/http://reocities.com/collegepark/plaza/9433/SMs.html Wayback, 9 April 2016]; [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009142705/https://www.geocities.ws/plarathas/SMs.html Wayback, 9 October 2026].</ref> On 10 October 2012 a Spanish hobby thread on labsk.net said SWCCG had little acceptance in Spain, perhaps because it was only in English.<ref name="labsk">[https://labsk.net/index.php?topic=95165.msg973702 Star Wars CCG, rediseñado], labsk.net, LeBastard (10 October 2012). Print view: [https://labsk.net/juegos-redisenados/star-wars-ccg-redisenado/?action=printpage labsk.net print].</ref>

== Fan translations ==

CardGuide Wiki tags Star Wars CCG as Language English, Japanese, Spanish and lists Premiere Limited OTHER LANGUAGES ES JP. Its Premiere Limited (ES) page is a title-translation checklist with empty packaging.<ref name="cardguide-es">[https://cardguide.fandom.com/wiki/Premiere_Limited_(Star_Wars_CCG)_(ES) Premiere Limited (Star Wars CCG) (ES)], CardGuide Wiki. [https://cardguide.fandom.com/wiki/Star_Wars_CCG Star Wars CCG] at CardGuide Wiki.</ref> Those titles do not match the 1998 booklet. The booklet prints '''Barrera Imperial''' and leaves Caller, Jawa, Blaster, and LIN-V8K in English. CardGuide lists names such as Imperial Barrera, Ilamador (Caller), Holandés (Dutch), and Beru Estofado (Beru Stew). That table is a fan checklist.

Players Committee PDFs titled ''gameterms_en_espanol.pdf'' and ''ds2_expansion_rules_en_espanol.pdf'' are 2009 fan translations by Renato Tenorio. They use '''Juego de Cartas Seleccionables''' for the game name. The 1998 booklet uses '''Juego de Cartas Coleccionables (SW-JCC)'''. Those PC files are a later volunteer glossary.<ref name="tenorio">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/wp/wp-content/uploads/2019/04/gameterms_en_espanol.pdf Equivalencias inglés – español], Renato Tenorio, version 1.5 (© 2009). [https://res.starwarsccg.org/wp/wp-content/uploads/2019/04/ds2_expansion_rules_en_espanol.pdf Death Star II rules supplement (Spanish)], Renato Tenorio (© 2009). Preserved copy of the Death Star II PDF: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009142831/https://res.starwarsccg.org/wp/wp-content/uploads/2019/04/ds2_expansion_rules_en_espanol.pdf Wayback, 9 October 2026]. Index: [https://www.starwarsccg.org/rules/ starwarsccg.org/rules/].</ref>
